items.reason: HD 99492 has no Multi-stars row, so its companion cannot be placed. Its name equals the system name and the Planet-host star of both planets, so the loader draws it at the origin and 83 Leo A goes round it.
items.notes: Every value except the component name, role, star count and planet-host columns is copied from Systems row 124. Cross-check: CLS (Rosenthal et al. 2021, ApJS 255, 8, Table 2; VizieR J/ApJS/255/8/table2, CPS 99492) gives Teff 4936.5 +/- 63.4 K, [Fe/H] 0.278 +/- 0.06, M 0.856 +/- 0.031, which agree with the Systems values. HD 99492 is physically the secondary: 83 Leo A is brighter (Gaia G 6.30 vs 7.27) and more massive (1.02 vs 0.86 Msun). It stays as the host because the system is filed under it and it hosts the planets. The Gaia DR3 parallax is 55.0618 mas, which gives 59.23 ly; the Systems value of 59.37 ly is 0.23% longer, which is within tolerance. The age is left blank because no age for HD 99492 was found. Brewer et al. 2016 give 4.6 (2.3-6.9) Gyr for its co-eval companion HD 99491, and the writer could adopt that as the system age with a note.

items.reason: 83 Leo A (HD 99491, G9 IV-V, 1.02 Msun) is the brighter wide companion of the planet host HD 99492 = 83 Leo B. It sits 28.17 arcsec away, which is 512.2 au projected (Gonzalez-Payo et al. 2024, A&A 689, A302, Table B.4). The Systems row lists HD 99492 as a single star.
items.notes:
The primary: 83 Leo A is the physical primary (the brighter and more massive star, and WDS component A). The system stays filed under HD 99492 because that is its Systems column A name and its planet host. The loader always draws the star named like the system at the origin, so HD 99491 must carry 'Separation from' = 'HD 99492'. The role follows the GJ 773 A precedent. If the writer would rather call HD 99491 'host', that is harmless to the loader, which does not read the role when the system name is a component. The separation must still point at HD 99492, and HD 99492's role should then become 'planet host'.

'Primary mass (M-sun)': 0.85 follows the practice of giving the origin star's mass. If the column is meant to hold the physical primary's mass, use 1.02.

Mass: Brewer et al. 2016 give an isochrone mass of 0.98 (0.96-1.00) and logL = -0.15 +/- 0.02 (0.71 Lsun). TIC v8.2 gives M 0.95, L 0.775, Teff 5438. CLS is preferred as the most recent refereed value.

L: the Gaia FLAME value, 0.745, falls between Brewer's 0.71 and TIC's 0.775, and matches the Rejected tab.

Class: WDS gives G7V and C05 (run 2) quoted Hipparcos K0IV. SIMBAD's G9IV-V is used.

WDS STF1540 AC (204.7 arcsec, pm +8/-18 mas/yr) is an optical background star, not a member. The system has two stars.

The Teff is odd: Fouque 2018 gives B (2842 K) as hotter than A (2810 K) despite the later class. Both are photometric. SIMBAD also lists 3167 K for UV Cet (Koleva & Vazdekis 2012). If the writer does not want an inferred L, leave L blank. The system then still draws, without bands.

items.notes:
The candidate's host is ambiguous in the paper: Table 2 gives a B solution (a = 0.274 au, 36 Mearth, listed first) and an A solution (0.283 au, 39 Mearth). The sheet uses B, which is kept, and the component name matches it exactly.

RV: Gaia DR3 gives B 10.25 +/- 3.24 km/s against A's 21.46 +/- 0.79. For a pair whose orbital speeds are a few km/s, an 11 km/s difference is impossible, so the Gaia RV for B (RUWE 10.45) is rejected. Fouque's 22.01 +/- 4.9 agrees with A. Kervella 2016 Sect. 3.3 gives UVES heliocentric RVs of +37.83 (A) and +40.29 (B) km/s, which disagree with Gaia and Fouque by about 16 km/s. They are not used, and I could not resolve the discrepancy.

Mass: Kervella 2016 gives 0.1195 +/- 0.0043 and Cifuentes 2025 0.118 +/- 0.045. GRAVITY (dynamical) is preferred.

The VizieR 10 pc census (Gonzalez-Payo et al., J/MNRAS/549/G838 table C3) repeats a = 5.459 au, P = 26.38 yr, ref 2024A&A...685L...9G.

incidental_finds: GJ 65 b source volume: the Unconfirmed row 116 'Source / discovery reference' and Sources & Provenance row 4582 cite 'A&A 695, L9'. Crossref gives GRAVITY Collaboration 2024, A&A 685, L9, doi:10.1051/0004-6361/202449547 (arXiv:2404.08746, accepted 20 March 2024). The bibcode 2024A&A...685L...9G in the VizieR 10 pc census agrees. https://api.crossref.org/works?query.bibliographic=Astrometric+detection+of+a+Neptune-mass+candidate+planet+in+the+nearest+M-dwarf+binary+system+GJ65

GJ 65 distance: Systems row 377 has 8.87 ly, from BL Cet's Gaia DR3 parallax 367.71 mas (RUWE 12.37). UV Cet's own Gaia parallax is 373.84 mas (RUWE 10.45), and GRAVITY 2024 Table 1 adopts 371.92 +/- 0.42 mas (Kervella et al. 2022), which gives 8.770 ly. The Unconfirmed row 116 'Catalogue distance (ly)' of 8.724 corresponds to UV Cet's 373.84 mas. Recommend 8.77 ly. https://arxiv.org/abs/2404.08746

GJ 65 B Gaia DR3 radial velocity (10.25 +/- 3.24 km/s) is inconsistent with BL Cet's 21.46 +/- 0.79 for a bound 5.5 au pair. Kervella et al. 2016 (A&A 593, A127, Sect. 3.3) quote UVES heliocentric RVs of +37.83 / +40.29 km/s, 16 km/s off both Gaia and Fouque 2018 (19.82 / 22.01). One of these zero points is wrong. This is worth a note if the RV is ever used for GJ 65's space velocity. https://arxiv.org/abs/1607.04351

61 Cyg A metallicity: Systems row 364 has [Fe/H] = +0.224 (Gaia DR3 GSP-Phot mh_gspphot 0.2244). Spectroscopy gives CLS -0.323 +/- 0.072, Luck & Heiter 2005 -0.20 +/- 0.10, Tomkin & Lambert 1999 -0.43, and Gaia's own GSP-Spec -0.50. The sign is wrong. Other Systems rows whose [Fe/H] came from GSP-Phot may share the problem. https://vizier.cds.unistra.fr/viz-bin/VizieR-5?-source=J/ApJS/255/8/table2&CPS=201091
HIP 87773 class: the sheet has 'K7' (WDS). SIMBAD gives K6V (Gray et al. 2003, AJ 126, 2048), a spectroscopic type. https://simbad.cds.unistra.fr/simbad/sim-id?Ident=HIP+87773

El-Badry, Rix & Heintz 2021 (VizieR J/MNRAS/506/2269) gives published projected separations for Gaia wide pairs, including TOI hosts that Gonzalez-Payo et al. 2024 does not cover. It could replace the 'COMPUTED here, not published' separations on the GJ 1177 B (row 92) and GJ 773 A (row 94) rows, if those pairs are in it (not checked).
